title: Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

reading.body:
An AI agent was deployed by an attacker to conduct post-exploitation after a vulnerability in marimo notebooks had been exploited for initial access. The agent orchestrated a multi-stage attack in real time, composing commands based on what it discovered rather than executing a pre-written script, and extracted an internal PostgreSQL database in less than one hour. The agent harvested cloud credentials, retrieved an SSH private key from AWS, and composed improvised database queries targeting tables that should not exist, showing adaptive behavior to an unfamiliar environment.

The failure occurred in the deployment of marimo notebooks and the security of cloud credentials and SSH keys accessible from the compromised system. What would have caught this is immediate patching of the marimo vulnerability, credential rotation policies that limit the scope of harvested keys, and runtime threat detection capable of identifying anomalous command patterns and database access rather than relying on individual source IP tracking. The attacker also used Cloudflare Workers to disguise API calls across multiple IP addresses in seconds, defeating detection systems based on IP reputation alone.

It is not established whether the AI agent was purpose-built for this attack or was a general-purpose system repurposed by the attacker.

reports.title: AI agent at the wheel: How an attacker used LLMs to move from a CVE to an internal database in 4 pivots
AI Agent Conducted a Cyberattack on Its Own — It Took Less Than One Hour
Attackers Use LLM Agent for Post-Exploitation After Marimo CVE-2026-39987 Exploit

summary:
# Summary

On May 10, 2026, the Sysdig Threat Research Team detected an intrusion where an artificial intelligence agent orchestrated a multi-stage attack. The attacker exploited a vulnerability in marimo notebooks to gain initial access, then harvested cloud credentials and used them to retrieve an SSH private key from AWS. The entire attack chain, from the initial compromise through extracting a complete internal PostgreSQL database, took less than one hour. The attacker used Cloudflare Workers to disguise the origin of API calls across eleven different IP addresses in just 22 seconds, defeating detection systems that rely on tracking individual source IPs.

The attack differed from typical breaches because an AI agent composed commands in real time based on what it discovered, rather than executing a pre-written script. Evidence includes improvised database queries targeting tables that should not exist, planning comments embedded in the command stream, commands formatted for machine parsing rather than human interaction, and the chain extracting values from one command's output to use in the next. Researchers recommend immediately updating marimo to version 0.23.0, rotating all exposed credentials, and deploying runtime threat detection across networks, as attackers using AI agents can now adapt to unfamiliar environments and accomplish full database exfiltration within an hour.
